action_items: MINOR: AdminKiosk.jsx writes BOTH the scope-namespaced key (efc.kiosk.<scope>.<key>) AND the legacy un-namespaced key (efc.kiosk.<key>) — because notify.js still reads the un-namespaced form. This makes cross-tenant cleanliness dependent on last-write-wins timing: when a super-admin browses to a mess-owner impersonated kiosk and back, the un-namespaced keys get overwritten with the new scope's values, which is good. But if notify.js is ever fired while the CMS fetch is in flight or races another tab, stale greetings could still play once. Consider migrating notify.js (announceCheckinSuccess) to read localStorage['efc.kiosk.' + localStorage.getItem('efc.kiosk.active_scope') + '.<key>'] to eliminate the legacy path entirely.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/subscription_tabs.py is clean: single query with a filter switch on tab, batch user hydration via $in, MongoDB _id excluded. days_left clamp mirrors SubscriberDashboard iter-140 coherency exactly. Sort direction correctly flips DESC only for expired tab.
The 'active' tab uses end_date > now+3d as a STRICT greater-than while 'expiring' uses <= now+3d — no overlap, no double-counting. Good.

admin.py active_dining/active_tiffin split is O(N) with a users find_one per subscription — same pattern as pre-171 active_subs counter, so no regression, but this is a candidate for a future bulk-lookup refactor if active-sub counts grow to hundreds.
SubscriptionTabs.jsx prime-loads all three counts in parallel on mount then re-fetches full rows on tab click — good UX, no waterfall. Empty state and loading state both have dedicated testids.
AdminKiosk.jsx dual-write to legacy + scoped keys is documented in a comment, but the un-namespaced legacy key is still the READ path for notify.js — see action item above.
